fieldMarks: Thickset, 102–152 cm long, 6.8–15 kg, with short legs and a neck as thick as the head
Inconspicuous ears; thick, tapered tail about a third of body length
Only the hind feet are webbed
Prime fur black-brown with a slightly paler belly and grayish chin and throat
behavior: Signs are seen more often than the animal: well-used overland trails between waters, rolling areas, twisted grass tufts and scent-post scats
Runs and slides on snow and ice, and slides on mud
Eats fish, mollusks, crabs, frogs and other aquatic prey; small items eaten at the surface, larger ones ashore
Travels in family groups or bachelor-male groups over large, overlapping, usually linear home ranges
habitat: Streams, lakes, ponds, swamps, marshes, beaver flowages, estuaries and exposed Pacific coastline; dens in abandoned beaver lodges, burrows, log jams and thickets near water.
range: Throughout most of North America north of Mexico except the extreme southwestern U.S.; extirpated from large areas of the interior U.S. and reintroduced in some states.
